title: Trade Entry Checker – Parameter-based entry signal tool

requirements.text: Add a new 'Trade Entry Checker' tab/view in the app (alongside the existing tabs in App.tsx) that allows the user to input the following parameters for a potential trade: Current Price, EMA20, EMA50, EMA200, RSI (0–100), ATR (absolute value), MACD Direction (dropdown: Bullish / Neutral / Bearish), and Trade Direction (Long / Short). All input labels and UI text must be in English.

quotes: kannst du sowas in die App mit einbauen, wo man bestimmte Parameter eingibt, und die App dann sagt, ob man einsteigen soll oder lieber nicht?

acceptanceCriteria: A new 'Trade Entry Checker' tab is visible in the main navigation.
The view contains numeric inputs for Current Price, EMA20, EMA50, EMA200, ATR, and RSI.
A dropdown allows selecting MACD Direction: Bullish, Neutral, or Bearish.
A toggle or radio allows selecting trade direction: Long or Short.
All labels, placeholders, and button text are in English.

requirements.text: Implement a purely frontend rule engine that evaluates the submitted parameters and produces a clear entry recommendation. For Long entries evaluate: (1) EMA trend alignment: EMA20 > EMA50 > EMA200; (2) Price proximity: Current Price is within 1× ATR above EMA20 (not overextended); (3) RSI not overbought: RSI < 65; (4) MACD Direction is Bullish or Neutral. For Short entries mirror the conditions (EMA20 < EMA50 < EMA200, price within 1× ATR below EMA20, RSI > 35, MACD Bearish or Neutral). Each condition is evaluated independently and displayed as a checklist row with a pass/fail indicator.

quotes: die App dann sagt, ob man einsteigen soll oder lieber nicht

acceptanceCriteria: After submitting the form, each of the four conditions is shown as a labeled checklist row with a green checkmark (pass) or red cross (fail) icon.
The number of conditions met is counted and displayed (e.g., '3 / 4 conditions met').
If all 4 conditions pass, a prominent green 'Entry looks good – proceed with caution' message is shown.
If 3 conditions pass, a yellow 'Marginal setup – wait for better confirmation' message is shown.
If 2 or fewer conditions pass, a red 'Do not enter – setup not confirmed' message is shown.
The overextension check uses the ATR value: entry is flagged if Current Price > EMA20 + 1×ATR (Long) or Current Price < EMA20 − 1×ATR (Short).

requirements.text: Below the checklist, display a short plain-English explanation for each failed condition describing why it disqualifies the entry and what the user should wait for. For example: if RSI ≥ 65 on a Long, show 'RSI is overbought (≥65) – wait for RSI to pull back below 60 before entering.' If price is overextended beyond 1× ATR above EMA20, show 'Price is overextended above EMA20 – wait for a pullback to EMA20 level before entering.'

quotes: die App dann sagt, ob man einsteigen soll oder lieber nicht

acceptanceCriteria: Each failed condition has a corresponding explanation text rendered beneath the checklist.
Passed conditions show no extra explanation text (or a brief green confirmation).
All explanation texts are in English.
Explanations reference the actual input values where meaningful (e.g., 'RSI is 72, which is above the 65 threshold').

requirements.text: Add a visual summary card at the top of the Trade Entry Checker results that shows: the selected trade direction (Long/Short) with a colored badge, the asset implied by the inputs (free-text asset name input field added to the form), and the overall verdict (Go / Wait / No-Go) with traffic-light color coding (green / yellow / red) and a matching icon.
acceptanceCriteria: A summary card is displayed above the checklist after evaluation.
The card shows the asset name entered by the user.
The card shows the selected direction (Long in green tones, Short in red tones).
The verdict badge is green for 'Go', yellow for 'Wait', and red for 'No-Go'.
The card is rendered before the per-condition checklist.

requirements.text: The Trade Entry Checker form must include a 'Reset' button that clears all inputs and the result, and a 'Check Entry' submit button that triggers evaluation. Inputs should be validated: numeric fields must be positive numbers, RSI must be 0–100, ATR must be > 0. Show inline validation errors in English if the user submits with missing or invalid values.
acceptanceCriteria: Submitting with any empty required field shows an inline error message next to that field.
Submitting with RSI outside 0–100 shows an inline error.
Submitting with ATR ≤ 0 shows an inline error.
The Reset button clears all fields and hides the results panel.
The Check Entry button triggers evaluation and scrolls/focuses the results.

constraints: All rule evaluation logic must be purely frontend (no backend calls required for this feature).
Do not modify any files listed in frontend.immutablePaths.
All user-facing text in the new view must be in English.
nonGoals: No real-time price or indicator data fetching – all values are manually entered by the user.
No integration with Hyperliquid API for EMA/RSI/ATR data in this feature.
No backend storage of entry checks or results.
No charting or candlestick rendering inside the Trade Entry Checker.

The uploaded image (ICT models: HTF POI, FVG, OTE, Box Setup) is for inspiration/context only – the checker does not need to implement ICT model logic, only the EMA/RSI/ATR/MACD rules discussed in the conversation.
